summary: Classical-stage supplement to the accepted T.1 packet. Imports its 43 classical nodes and the exact U.1 matrix/elementary owners, adds the trivial-action criterion and an injective column/row API, and supplies seven scoped proof refinements closing the old classical matrix, colimit, centre, classification and lifted-relation inputs. Recognition, Hopf and the integral quotient-bar package retain their existing owner ids. Six existing planets are retained, with no new planet. All implementation status is unchecked; this pass awaits independent review.

nodes.title: Centrality and a specified trivial coefficient action
nodes.statement: Let S be a marked extension 1 → A → E → G → 1, with A commutative. Fix a multiplicative distributive G-action on A and assume g • a = a for every g,a. Then the range of S.inl lies in the centre of E if and only if TauCeti.GroupExtension.InducesAction S holds. This is a statement about the actual conjugation action of S, not just an arbitrarily chosen trivial ambient action.
hypotheses: G and E are groups and A is a commutative group.
S is the actual pinned GroupExtension A E G.
The specified ambient G-action on A is trivial, for every g,a.
proofSteps: For the forward implication, conjAct_eq_one_of_le_center makes conjugation on A the identity. Together with triviality of the specified action this is exactly InducesAction.

For the reverse implication, InducesAction and triviality imply S.conjAct e a = a. The pinned inl_conjAct_comm identifies e S.inl(a) e inverse with S.inl(a). Multiply on the right by e and apply mem_center_iff.
No splitting or section is used. The existing inducesAction_iff_smul_eq_self assumes centrality and cannot alone provide the reverse implication.
acceptance: The product extension A × G → G satisfies the criterion for the trivial action.
The nonsplit central extension C4 → C2 satisfies the criterion too; trivial induced action does not imply splitting.
For C3 ↪ S3 → C2, conjugation inverts C3. With an ambient trivial action the extension fails InducesAction and fails centrality.

nodes.title: Injective column and row normal forms in Steinberg groups
nodes.statement: For an associative unital ring R, n ≥ 3 and an index t, define rho_t from the additive group of vectors (v_i) indexed by i ≠ t to St_n(R) by the product of x_it(v_i). These roots commute, so the order is immaterial and rho_t is an injective additive-to-multiplicative homomorphism. Its matrix image is I + sum_i E_it(v_i). Its composite into St(R) is also injective. The row analogue eta_t(v) = product_i x_ti(v_i) has the same assertions. For a,b distinct and both different from t, conjugation by x_ab(c) replaces column coordinate v_a by v_a + c v_b, and row coordinate v_b by v_b − v_a c. These are left and right multiplications in the displayed order.
hypotheses: R is an associative unital ring; neither commutativity nor nontriviality is assumed.
n ≥ 3; vectors have exactly n−1 coordinates, omitting t.
For the normalization formulas a ≠ b, a ≠ t and b ≠ t. Opposite roots are excluded.
proofSteps: Use the nonchaining Steinberg relation to commute all column roots, and additivity to obtain rho_t(v+w)=rho_t(v)rho_t(w). The same-root case is included. Define its finite image subgroup by its range.

The imported elementary-matrix product has all cross terms zero, since t differs from every row index. Thus the matrix image is I + sum_i E_it(v_i). Reading entry (i,t) recovers v_i, proving injectivity in finite rank. The row proof reads (t,i).

Stable injectivity of these particular subgroups follows by composing with St(R) → E(R) ≤ GL(R): U.1 supplies injective finite GL transition maps and its injective stage-to-stable embeddings. Do not infer injectivity of the entire St_n(R) → St(R).

Conjugate each column root using the nonchaining or forward-chaining relation. Only x_bt(v_b) changes, by the additional commuting factor x_at(c v_b). For rows use the reverse-chaining relation on x_ta(v_a), producing x_tb(−v_a c). Other row roots commute.
These formulas show that a word using indices different from t normalizes both image subgroups. Ring maps act coordinatewise. Stabilization extends vectors by zero and preserves t and these formulas.
acceptance: Coordinate recovery, including over noncommutative rings, proves finite and stable injectivity without a stable Steinberg embedding hypothesis.
Both normalization identities retain the stated index conditions and coefficient order.
A kernel word whose indices omit t has commutators with column and row roots in these injective subgroups; this is the input to the inherited centre theorem.

api.name: Steinberg.column
api.statement: rho_t(v)=product over i≠t of x_it(v_i), with commuting factors and fixed finite index type.

api.name: Steinberg.row
api.statement: eta_t(v)=product over i≠t of x_ti(v_i), with commuting factors.

api.name: Steinberg.column_add
api.statement: rho_t(v+w)=rho_t(v)rho_t(w); the identical row law also holds.

api.name: Steinberg.column_basis
api.statement: rho_t of the vector supported at i with value r is x_it(r); row basis evaluates to x_ti(r).

api.name: Steinberg.phi_column
api.statement: The image under phi_n is I+sum_i E_it(v_i); row image is I+sum_i E_ti(v_i).

api.name: Steinberg.column_injective
api.statement: rho_t and eta_t are injective, and remain injective after mapping to stable St(R).

api.name: Steinberg.column_conj
api.statement: For a,b≠t and a≠b, x_ab(c)rho_t(v)x_ab(c) inverse equals rho_t(v with v_a increased by c v_b).

api.name: Steinberg.row_conj
api.statement: Under the same hypotheses conjugation increases row coordinate v_b by −v_a c.

api.name: Steinberg.column_map
api.statement: Ring maps act on every vector entry; index stabilization adds zero entries. Row maps satisfy the same laws.

uses.how: Normalization places the kernel commutators in column and row subgroups, where matrix-coordinate injectivity forces them to be trivial.
A fresh column and row let every old root be expressed as a commutator through a new index.

tests.name: column_zero
tests.statement: For any n,t, rho_t(0)=1 and eta_t(0)=1; over the zero ring both image groups are trivial.

tests.name: column_integer_coordinates
tests.statement: In rank three over Z, with t=3 and vector (2,3), phi_3(rho_3(v))=I+2E13+3E23. Thus rho_3(v) is not identity.

tests.name: column_noncommutative_order
tests.statement: Over R=M2(Z), for the outer rank-three column t=3, take c=E12 and v_2=E21. Conjugation by x_12(c) adds E11 to v_1, not E22.

tests.name: row_noncommutative_order
tests.statement: Over R=M2(Z), take row t=3, c=E12 and v_1=E21. Conjugation by x_12(c) adds −E22 to v_2, not −E11.

tests.name: column_stable_nonzero
tests.statement: Over Z, the stable image of rho_3(1,0)=x_13(1) has matrix entry (1,3)=1 and is nonidentity.

tests.name: column_opposite_root_exclusion
tests.statement: Over Z, conjugating e_13(1) by e_31(1) gives a matrix with a nonzero (3,1) entry and changed diagonal entries. It is not in the column subgroup; the normalizer formula cannot include a=t or b=t.

proofSteps: Let y in the stable kernel and fix any generator x_kl(r). Choose a representative word for y and a common rank containing the word and k,l, and then a fresh index t. No occurrence of t is needed in the word.

By the column conjugation formula, that word normalizes the column subgroup P_t. Hence [y,x_kt(r)] lies in P_t. Its stable matrix image is identity because y is in the kernel. Stable column injectivity forces the commutator to be identity.
The row argument gives [y,x_tl(1)]=1. Since x_kl(r)=[x_kt(r),x_tl(1)], y commutes with the tested generator. All stable generators generate, so the kernel is central.

Conversely a central Steinberg element maps into the centre of E(R) by surjectivity. The exact U.1 stable-elementary-centre node says that even a stable GL element commuting with all E(R) is identity. Thus the centre lies in the kernel.
A subgroup of the centre is commutative; give the kernel its inherited commutative group structure.
acceptance: The fresh index lies beyond both a chosen word and the tested root.
The only injectivity used is the imported finite GL embedding and the proved column/row embedding.
No general finite-rank centrality claim follows.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.5.10 and its proof, printed pp.33–37 / PDF pp.41–45; Remark 1.5.11, printed p.37 / PDF p.45
sources.match: Classifies extensions for a fixed action and identifies the split class. The normalized-section implementation and quotient model are the actual pinned Tau Ceti declarations.

proofSteps: Let q:Y→St_n(R) be central and surjective, n≥5. Lifts of any one root differ by a central element, so their commutator with another lift is independent of the lift choices.

First prove exact commutation of lifted nonchaining roots. If u lifts x_ij(a), z lifts x_kl(b), j≠k and i≠l, choose t outside {i,j,k,l}. Choose v over x_it(1) and w over x_tj(a). The commutators [v,z] and [w,z] lie in the central kernel. Conjugation by z therefore fixes [v,w]. Since u differs from [v,w] centrally, [u,z]=1. This uses at most five indices.

For four distinct indices i,k,l,j, choose u over x_ik(a), v over x_kl(b), w over x_lj(c). Put C=[u,v], D=[v,w], e=[C,w], f=[u,D]. The first step gives [u,w]=[C,D]=1. The elements e and f both lie over x_ij(abc), and each commutes with u,v,w,C,D by the same step. Reordering uvw in two ways gives C D w v u and f e inverse C D w v u; cancellation gives e=f. Thus [[u,v],w]=[u,[v,w]] in precisely this root configuration. No unqualified metabelian Jacobi identity is assumed.

Define c_ij(a)=[lift(x_ik(1)),lift(x_kj(a))] with k≠i,j. Central lift independence is immediate. To replace k by another auxiliary l, use the preceding identity on lifts of x_il(1), x_lk(1), x_kj(a). Its two sides are exactly the two definitions, since their intermediate commutators differ from any chosen lift only centrally.

For additivity, choose u over x_ik(1), v over x_kj(a), w over x_kj(b). The first step gives [v,w]=1 and says v commutes with [u,w], whose image has root (i,j). Then [u,vw]=[u,v] v[u,w]v inverse=c_ij(a)c_ij(b). The left side is c_ij(a+b). Setting a=b=0 gives c_ij(0)=1.

For the forward relation on distinct i,j,l, choose a fourth k. Apply the four-index identity to lifts of x_ik(1),x_kj(a),x_jl(b). Its left side is [c_ij(a),c_jl(b)] and its right side is c_il(ab). Swapping the roots gives the reverse relation c_kj(−ba), using [x,y] inverse=[y,x] and c_kj(r) inverse=c_kj(−r). All nonchaining relations follow from the first step.

All presentation relations now hold exactly in Y. The presentation lift sends x_ij(a) to c_ij(a), and its composite with q is identity on generators, hence is a homomorphic section. Finite perfectness is separate and holds already for n≥3.
Only if phi_n:St_n(R)→E_n(R) is separately central may the inherited perfect-and-splitting recognition lemma turn this into a finite universal central extension.
acceptance: All three commutator index cases and additivity are checked, including a fourth-index choice and the fifth-index commutation argument.
The noncommutative reverse coefficient is −ba.
The theorem is splitting over St_n(R), not unconditional finite centrality of phi_n.

proofSteps: The Steinberg generators are commutators through a third index, so finite St_n and stable St are perfect. The stable map is central and surjective by the refined centre and stabilization arguments.

Given any central extension q:Y→St(R), pull it back along each stage map St_n(R)→St(R), n≥5. Each pullback is central and surjective even if the stage map is not injective, and finite-rank splitting gives a section.

View the sections as maps St_n(R)→Y over the stage map. The next-stage section composed with stabilization and the current section give two sections of the same pullback over St_n(R). Finite perfectness and perfect-extension-rigidity make them equal.
Use the cofinal n≥5 subsystem and the pinned homomorphism colimit lift to produce St(R)→Y. Its composite with q is identity on all stage generators. Thus every central extension of St(R) splits.
Apply split-central-extension-universal. The imported uce-kernel-h2 gives K2(R)≅H2(E(R);Z); imported uce-lift and uce-kernel-h2-natural give naturality in every unital ring homomorphism.
Recognition gives superperfectness of St(R), the output consumed by V.1. No plus construction or Hurewicz argument enters this algebraic proof.
acceptance: Pullback surjectivity, compatible sections and colimit evaluation are all accounted for.
The statement holds for every associative unital ring.
Ring maps on K2 agree with the actual H2 map under the chosen canonical comparison.

sourceIssues.locator: Exercise III.5.2, printed p.228 / PDF p.236, author combined draft dated 29 August 2013
sourceIssues.printed: After defining a column map on R^(n−1), the exercise labels its image using R^n. It also labels the triangular subgroup generated by roots i<j as lower triangular.
sourceIssues.correction: The column subgroup is the image of R^(n−1), omitting the chosen column index. Under e_ij(r)=I+rE_ij, the i<j roots generate upper unitriangular matrices.
sourceIssues.reason: There are exactly n−1 indices i≠n. In rank three, e_12(1) over Z has a nonzero entry above the diagonal, contradicting the lower-triangular description. The full triangular-subgroup development is not used by this stage.

sourceIssues.locator: Exercise III.5.7, printed p.229 / PDF p.237, author combined draft dated 29 August 2013, first assertion
sourceIssues.printed: The exercise asserts that the composite of two central extensions is a central extension without a perfectness hypothesis on the intermediate group.
sourceIssues.correction: The assertion used here requires the intermediate group X to be perfect. The exercise’s subsequent universal-source application meets that hypothesis. Retain the existing parent central-extension-comp statement with this condition.
sourceIssues.reason: Let Y be the upper-unitriangular 3-by-3 group over F3, rho:Y→X=F3² forget the central coordinate, and pi:X→G=F3 project onto the first coordinate. Both maps are surjective with central kernels. But b=(0,1,0) is in the composite kernel and does not commute with a=(1,0,0): their commutator is (0,0,1). Thus the composite kernel is not central.
sourceIssues.known: No published correction was verified; no novelty is claimed. The parent blueprint already supplies the needed perfect-intermediate hypothesis, and this supplement records the source error explicitly.
